transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-24 16:00 PDT
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marco Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CinderBox Platform Eng), Ethan Cole (CinderBox SRE), Marta Ruiz (CinderBox Eng Manager)

Summary:
Quick deep-dive into Redwood Console tracing and request playback for debugging high p95 latency spikes; discuss request logs, KV cache miss patterns, and error triage flow. Customers asked about private deployment telemetry, audit logs, and cost impact of continuous tracing.

Topics:
- Trace playback & request inspector
- Error hunting flow and structured request logs
- KV cache / prefix cache debugging
- Private VPC telemetry and audit log retention
- Next steps: repro trace, SOC2 docs, pilot benchmark

Transcript:
[00:00] Lina: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Lina from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. we got Marco from our SE team who will walk through the console sleuth flow for request forensics. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya: Good, thanks. we had some p95 spikes last month that we haven't been able to consistently reproduce, so excited to see the playback tools.
[00:12] Ethan: Yeah hi, I'm Ethan, SRE. main concern: we need fast root-cause without shipping large amounts of logs off-site; also curious about retention options and encryption.
[00:20] Marco: Great — I'll share my screen, i might call out a few things by name, and please stop me if you want more detail. (screen share starts) okay starting in Console -> Requests -> playback, this is a synthetic view but follows the same schema you'll see in your account.
[00:35] Marco: you'll see each request row, status, model variant, latencies, and a "trace" link — clicking opens the request inspector which reconstructs the entire request lifecycle: routing, batching, kv cache hit/miss, and kernel fallback if applicable.
[00:50] Marta: Quick q — how accurate is the KV cache hit annotation? we saw hit rates reported but still large token generation times.
[00:55] Marco: good question — hits are inferred from prefix match and the recorded kv lookups; there are edge cases where partial prefix matches show as "probable hit" in the UI. sometimes the transcription or the labeling might say "k v cache" which is just the ASR artifact, sorry about that.
[01:10] Priya: ha, yes we noticed weird labels in earlier exports. can the playback show intermediate model fallbacks? like if it falls from 8-bit quant to a CPU slow path?
[01:20] Marco: yes — the inspector shows fallbacks with timestamps. we annotate kernel selection and device placement. fallback events are highlighted in orange; you can expand to see stack traces and the config used at the time.
[01:36] Ethan: Does the trace include payloads or just metadata? our legal team is picky about PII leaving the VPC.
[01:43] Lina: We have options — for Hosted we redact payloads by default in the UI, but for Private deployments you can enable full request retention locally. we'll send the private deployment telemetry guide after this call.
[01:55] Marco: also, you can toggle the "payload view" if your role has permission. RBAC controls in Console prevent accidental exposure; all access is recorded in audit logs with KMS-encrypted keys.
[02:10] Priya: good. let's dig into an example: on 2026-06-03 at 03:14 UTC we saw a spike — we uploaded the sample request id in the shared doc.
[02:22] Marco: pulling that id now... okay seeing the request. timeline shows 3 phases: pre-processing (tokenization), model serving, post-processing (prompt templating). model serving had a 1.2s tail at p99.
[02:36] Marco: selecting the "detailed trace" — aha, there's a KV cache miss followed by an extra roundtrip to the cache on a different node — that's a classic cross-shard miss. the playback annotates the DNS/Node id but sometimes the hostname is truncated in the speech transcription.
[02:55] Marta: cross-shard miss, hmm — do you do automatic replication for hot prefixes?
[03:01] Marco: we do multiple strategies — hot prefix replication and smart routing. but replication has CPU/memory tradeoffs; Redwood Optimize can recommend replication thresholds based on your access pattern.
[03:16] Priya: Is Optimize a separate billing item?
[03:18] Lina: it's an add-on that can be run as an evaluation rule set; we can provide a cost/benefit run for your traffic profile.
[03:26] Ethan: our main asker: can we run a live replay inside our VPC so nothing leaves our network? we want to replay with the same QPS and measure tail latency.
[03:34] Marco: yes — Private deployment supports on-prem replay. the Console has a "replay job" that will run the trace set against a pinned model variant on your dedicated pool. logs stay local if configured that way.
[03:46] Priya: what's the observability overhead of continuous tracing? we don't want a 10% QPS penalty.
[03:52] Marco: continuous tracing is sampled by default. you can enable full traces for a subset. sampling configs can be per-route, per-token, or by percentage. we estimate ~1-3% overhead at 10% sampling, but full traces at high qps will add overhead.
[04:08] Lina: for compliance, we also provide configurable retention windows and an exportable audit trail. we'll include the SOC2 excerpt that maps to audit log retention.
[04:16] Ethan: also, our security team asked about HSM integration for signing logs.
[04:21] Marco: HSM/KMS integrations are supported for Private — we have examples for AWS KMS and HashiCorp Vault in the docs.
[04:29] Priya: can we annotate traces with our internal ticket ids for faster triage?
[04:33] Marco: yes, the request inspector supports adding metadata tags either via headers or Console annotations — those show up in the trace timeline and are searchable.
[04:45] Marta: any pitfalls we should watch for when running the replay? like tokenization differences between SDK versions?
[04:52] Marco: absolutely — tokenizer mismatches can produce different token counts and change latency. we record the exact tokenizer hash and SDK version in the trace metadata, so compare those first.
[05:05] Priya: we saw a case where model quantization changed behavior between versions and caused higher tail latency.
[05:11] Marco: that happens — the console also stores model config snapshots per request; you can diff snapshots to see config drift.
[05:20] Lina: quick pause — i'm noting action items and will recap at the end.
[05:25] Ethan: a quick question about the trace export format — is it JSONL, or some proprietary binary?
[05:30] Marco: trace exports are JSONL with schema v2. we also provide a viz link for quick sharing internally. note that exported payloads are redacted unless you request full exports and enable private retention.
[05:43] Priya: okay let's try a live repro. Marco, can you run a quick KV-cache micro-repro now? even a short run would be helpful.
[05:50] Marco: I can kick off a small synthetic that simulates cross-shard lookup pattern — i'll run for a couple minutes, capture traces, and upload the URL.
[05:58] Marco: starting synthetic run... (few seconds) done — results are uploaded to the shared folder. the run shows a few cross-shard misses and one kernel fallback event.
[06:10] Priya: saw it — that fallback lines up with an older runtime that lacked the newer attention kernel. do you have guidance on toggling those kernels? we don't want to break quality.
[06:20] Marco: kernel toggles are handled by model variant flags. Redwood's rollout flow supports canarying a kernel change with automatic fallback if latency regresses.
[06:30] Marta: how do we instrument our app to annotate failures so the Console surfaces them as errors rather than unknowns?
[06:36] Marco: use the SDK's error mapping: attach trace_id and error_code in the wrapper, we ingest those in structured logs. also the Console links to error grouping and you can create alerts off of that.
[06:48] Priya: any limitations with multi-tenant dedicated pools and trace correlation?
[06:52] Marco: we expose tenant ids in the trace metadata and map them to routes. for dedicated pools tenant isolation is enforced; trace correlation will still show tenant-scoped events only if your role allows it.
[07:05] Ethan: can we get per-token cost breakdown in the trace? helps us decide between quantization options.
[07:12] Marco: yes — cost is estimated per-request and token-level cost buckets are available in the trace view; Optimize can simulate cost changes from quantization and batching.
[07:25] Priya: perfect. next steps from our side: we'll collect relevant request ids and set up a pilot window next week.
[07:32] Lina: great — i'll follow up with the SOC2 and private deployment notes and a pricing ballpark. Marco will share the synthetic run link and a short how-to on running replays.
[07:40] Marco: uploading the synthetic run link to the shared doc now: https://redwood.shares/trace/ff-98321/synth1 (note: demo link, will send real artifact)
[07:50] Marta: thanks. one last ask — can Redwood surface a replay run summary as a PDF for our execs?
[07:56] Marco: we can generate a replay summary PDF via Console export; include it in the pilot artifact bundle.
[08:05] Priya: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[08:08] Lina: cool, quick recap of action items then we'll wrap.
[08:12] Lina: Marco — run a KV-cache repro and share traces (due 6/30). Lina — send SOC2 + private deploy docs (due 6/26). Priya — provide request samples and qps targets (due 6/29). we'll plan the pilot run for first week of July.
[08:30] Ethan: sounds good, thanks all.
[08:33] Meeting end

Shared artifacts mentioned:
- SOC2 excerpt: https://redwood.docs/soc2-excerpt
- Private deployment telemetry guide: https://redwood.docs/private-telemetry
- Synthetic run (demo): https://redwood.shares/trace/ff-98321/synth1

Notes on transcription quality: there are occasional ASR artifacts ("k v" vs "KV"), and some hostnames truncated; speaker attributions were manually corrected where obvious.

End of transcript.
